content.title: ‘Do Not Travel’: The Most Dangerous Countries for Americans Right Now
content.text: The U.S. State Department is warning Americans to completely avoid traveling to several countries right now. The agency's latest "Do Not Travel" advisories highlight destinations that are considered especially dangerous for reasons ranging from war to crime. Here is the full list of the countries that people from the United States should stay away from right now.The Countries on the Latest ListBright airport display screen highlighting numerous flight cancellations and delays, representing the real-world impact of high-risk travel advisories on U.S. citizens.Photo: Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images (Photo: Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images)At all times, the United States government tracks which countries are dangerous for Americans to travel to. The State Department then assigns the most perilous locations the "Level 4: Do Not Travel" designation. As of March 2026, the following 22 countries are under the most serious travel advisories for Americans.The State Department's Current Full List of "Level 4: Do Not Travel" Countries:AfghanistanBelarusBurkina FasoBurma (Myanmar)Central African RepublicGazaHaitiIranIraqLebanonLibyaMaliNigerNorth KoreaRussiaSomaliaSouth SudanSudanSyriaUkraineVenezuelaYemenThe State Department's website lists why each country is under a "Do Not Travel" warning and when each travel advisory was originally issued. Of the current Level 4 warnings, the longest-running one listed on the website was issued for Ukraine on November 11, 2024. The reasons for each country's warning vary, including unrest, crime, health, kidnapping or hostage taking, terrorism, wrongful detention, and "other."What a ‘Level 4: Do Not Travel’ Actually MeansThe State Department issues travel warnings that range from Level 1 to Level 4. A website called The U.S. News explains what each level means. For example, it describes the least serious advisories as meaning: "There is some risk in any international travel. Conditions in other countries may differ from those in the United States and may change at any time."On the other hand, its explanation for what a Level 4 warning means proves how seriously Americans should take them."This is the highest advisory level due to a greater likelihood of life-threatening risks. During an emergency, the U.S. government may have very limited ability to provide assistance. The Department of State advises that U.S. citizens not travel to the country or to leave as soon as it is safe to do so. The Department of State provides additional advice for travelers in these areas in the Travel Advisory. Conditions in any country may change at any time."This story was originally published by Men's Journal on Mar 28, 2026, where it first appeared in the News section.
